movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column 30 Jun 20 -> column 30 Jun 21
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 4 bps in FY21 to 2.03% from 2.07% in FY20 (cash basis, continuing operations): the results book's performance summary prints 2.03 vs 2.07, (4)bpts, and states the margin "decreased 4 basis points on the prior year". Net interest income still rose $229m or 1% to $18,839m as average interest earning assets grew $32bn or 4% to $930bn, partly offset by the margin decline. The FY21 results presentation's full-year walk (207 → 203 bps, bars sum to -4) decomposes the move: Higher Liquids -4, Asset Pricing -2, Deposit Pricing & Funding -3, Capital & Other -2, Portfolio Mix +2, Basis Risk (incl RP) +3, Treasury & Markets +2. The slide headlines the walk "Flat ex liquids – pressure from lower interest rates, offset by favourable portfolio mix, lower wholesale funding costs". The FY20 book corroborates the 2.07% starting point. Context: the RBS divisional NIM fell 3 bps (2.60 vs 2.63) and the FY20 book also prints 2.08% including discontinued operations; neither supplies this movement.

drivers.narrative: Bar -4 bps. Book: 'Decreased margin by 4 basis points driven by increased lower yielding non-lending interest earning assets, including liquid assets.' Non-lending AIEA rose $20bn or 12% to $195bn, including a $17bn rise in average liquid asset balances on strong customer deposit growth. Slide qualifies: 'Minimal impact on NII'.

Bar -2 bps. Lower business lending margins (down 1 bp) from repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19; lower consumer finance margins (down 1 bp) from a reduced proportion of interest-earning credit card balances. Home lending flat: repricing +9 bps offset by switching to lower-margin loans -5 bps and competition -4 bps.

Bar -3 bps. Lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits mainly due to decreases in the cash rate (down 7 bps; slide shows -8), partly offset by higher replicating portfolio benefits (up 2 bps) and lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 bps); slide adds investment deposits +1 bp.

Bar -2 bps. Lower earnings on Group capital due to the falling interest rate environment (down 3 bps), partly offset by increased contribution from New Zealand (up 1 bp) reflecting lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix, partly offset by RBNZ cash rate cuts.

Bar +2 bps. Higher average deposit funding ratio (77% at Jun 2021 vs 71% at Jun 2020) from strong transaction and savings deposit growth, customers switching to at-call deposits and the TFF drawdown (up 4 bps), partly offset by unfavourable asset mix (down 2 bps) as higher-margin consumer finance balances declined.

Bar +3 bps. Margin rose on a decrease in the average spread between the 3-month bank bill swap rate and the 3-month overnight index swap rate, notwithstanding a structural reduction in basis-risk exposure from strong growth in cash-rate-linked deposits and a mix shift towards fixed-rate home loans.
Bar +2 bps. Higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets. The bank discloses no further sub-components for this driver.

disagreements.topic: Cash-rate impact within Deposit Pricing & Funding
disagreements.explanation: Both describe the same cash-rate-cut drag on transaction and savings deposit earnings; the results book narrative outranks the slide annotation, and the total funding bar (-3 bps) is identical in both framings.

The FY21 Group row and the walk are presented on a continuing-operations basis (slide footnote: 'Presented on a continuing operations basis'); the 2.08% variant includes discontinued operations and is context only.

limitations: The adopted walk is published in the results presentation; the results book states the same seven drivers in words with matching component figures but prints no walk chart of its own.

The -4 bps Higher Liquids bar is qualified by the bank as having 'minimal impact on NII' - it is a balance-sheet mix effect from deposit-funded liquid asset growth, not lost customer margin; NII still grew $229m or 1%.
The Group NIM row carries no cash/statutory label; it is reported here on the bank's primary (cash) basis, continuing operations, per the KPI table footnote.
The RBS divisional NIM (-3 bps) and the half-on-half move (2H21 2.04% vs 1H21 2.01%, +3 bps) are different comparisons and were excluded from the driver table.

Sub-component figures inside Asset Pricing, Funding and Capital & Other come from the book narrative and slide annotations; the slide's cash-rate figure (-8 bps) differs by 1 bp from the book's (-7 bps).
